records.finding: The gauge parity query {Metric:biz_inflight_value, GroupBy:[age_bucket,currency]} proved nothing: the only in-flight samples were stamped at res.Config.End == window.To, and a half-open [From,To) read excludes At==To on BOTH sides (memq drops At>=To; the promql adapter evaluates last_over_time at To-1ms), so sameSeries(empty,empty) passed while never exercising the gauge/last_over_time translation.
records.evidence: points := testkit.MetricsFromResult(res)  // gauge snapshot at res.Config.End == window.To
records.reason: Added testkit.MetricsFromResultAt(res, gaugeAt); the harness now snapshots the gauge one minute inside the window, plus a stall-scenario non-emptiness guard so the assertion can never silently go vacuous again. Named regression test: testkit/querier_test.go TestInFlightGaugeSnapshotVisibleWithinWindow (at-To invisible vs interior visible). The live harness now compares real non-empty gauge series.

records.finding: memq's gauge aggregate() took the single last sample across a GroupBy-collapsed group, so a query grouping several series (stage=capture and stage=settle collapsing into one age_bucket/currency group) returned one series' level instead of their sum — diverging from a real backend's sum by(g)(last_over_time(m)). Exposed once the gauge parity became non-vacuous.
records.evidence: var last *emit.MetricPoint; ... if last==nil || points[i].At.After(last.At) { last = &points[i] } // single sample, not per-series sum
records.reason: aggregate() now keys by canonical(full labels), carries each underlying series' last level before the boundary forward, and sums them (AggCount returns the series count). Single-series carry-forward (TestGaugeCarriesForward) is preserved. Named regression test: query/memq/memq_test.go TestGaugeSumsCollapsedSeries. Live Prometheus parity confirmed for both scenarios.

records.finding: The translate() doc comment described the pre-fix counter translation `sum by(g)(m @ To) - sum by(g)(m @ From)` and called one-end series an unhandled edge case, both untrue after this diff, which emits `<end> - (<start> or (<end>*0))` via last_over_time and handles one-end series with the or-fill.
records.evidence: //     `sum by(g)(m @ To) - sum by(g)(m @ From)`. ... series present at only one end are edge cases tracked in workspace-0ka.
records.reason: Doc comment rewritten to describe the current `<end> - (<start> or (<end>*0))` last_over_time translation, the -1ms symmetric boundary eval, and that a one-end series is handled (filled to 0).

records.finding: The golden CI job (HIGH-tier .github enforcement surface) could go green having asserted nothing: with SHORTFALL_GOLDEN=1 set, the harness still t.Skip()ed when Docker was absent/not running, and a skipped Go test exits 0 — a silent gate-weakening if the runner ever lacked a Docker daemon.
records.evidence: if _, err := exec.LookPath("docker"); err != nil { t.Skip("docker not found; ...") }
records.reason: With SHORTFALL_GOLDEN set (the explicit demand to run the gate), missing Docker or a dead daemon is now t.Fatal, not t.Skip; the no-env skip path (core CI, Docker-less dev) is preserved. The env-set path has no remaining reachable Skip, so the golden job cannot pass vacuously.
